s361.content:
Prosper was a layman and theologian from Aquitaine in Gaul who became the great defender of St. Augustine’s teaching on grace after Augustine’s death. He later worked in Rome, probably for Pope St. Leo the Great.

He gave the Church a famous principle: the law of prayer establishes the law of belief, meaning that how the Church prays shows what she believes.
s361.intercession: St. Prosper, pray for us. Help us to depend on God’s grace in everything. Amen.

s362.content:
Mesrop was an Armenian royal secretary who became a monk and missionary. Frustrated that his people had no written language, he created the Armenian alphabet around 405.

With the Catholicos St. Sahak, he translated the Bible into Armenian, and he founded schools across the country. Armenian literature begins with him.
s362.intercession: St. Mesrop, pray for us. Bless translators and teachers who bring God’s word to every people. Amen.

s363.content:
Severinus was a mysterious monk who appeared in Noricum, along the Danube in today’s Austria, as Roman rule collapsed. He never spoke of his origins.

He organized food for the starving, ransomed captives, negotiated with barbarian kings, and led the Roman population to safety. He founded monasteries and was revered as a prophet.
s363.intercession: St. Severinus, pray for us. Protect refugees and all who live through the collapse of their world. Amen.

s364.content:
Gelasius, a pope of African descent, was known for his learning, his austerity, and his generosity to the poor during famine.

In a famous letter to the Emperor Anastasius, he taught that the world is governed by two powers: the sacred authority of bishops and the royal power of rulers, each with its own sphere. The idea shaped Western thought on Church and state.
s364.intercession: Pope St. Gelasius, pray for us. Help leaders of Church and state to serve God and the common good. Amen.

s365.content:
Remigius was made bishop of Reims at about twenty-two and served for more than seventy years. On Christmas Day around 496 he baptized Clovis, king of the Franks, together with thousands of his warriors.

According to Gregory of Tours, he said to the king at the font: "Bow your head, proud Sicambrian. Adore what you have burned, and burn what you have adored."
s365.intercession: St. Remigius, pray for us. Bless France, and help all who are converted to give themselves wholly to Christ. Amen.

s366.content:
Fulgentius was a Roman tax official in North Africa who left his career after reading St. Augustine and became a monk. Chosen bishop of Ruspe, he was soon exiled to Sardinia by the Arian Vandal king, along with many other bishops.

In exile he wrote many works defending the Trinity and Augustine’s teaching on grace. He is often called "the pocket Augustine."
s366.intercession: St. Fulgentius, pray for us. Strengthen Christians in exile, and help us to love the truth about God. Amen.

s367.content:
Caesarius was a monk of Lérins who served as archbishop of Arles for forty years. He was the most popular preacher of his day, keeping his sermons short and practical so ordinary people could understand, and he had them copied and sent to other priests.

He founded a convent for his sister, St. Caesaria, and wrote one of the first rules for nuns. He presided over the Second Council of Orange in 529.
s367.intercession: St. Caesarius, pray for us. Bless preachers, and help them speak the Gospel plainly. Amen.

s368.content:
Finnian founded the monastery of Clonard in Ireland, which drew thousands of students. He is called "the Teacher of the Saints of Ireland."

Among his disciples were the "Twelve Apostles of Ireland," including St. Columba and St. Brendan the Navigator, who went on to found monasteries across Ireland and beyond. He died of plague.
s368.intercession: St. Finnian, pray for us. Bless all who teach, that their students may become saints. Amen.

s369.content:
Germanus was an abbot near Autun before becoming bishop of Paris. He gave so generously to the poor and to ransom captives that he was called "the Father of the Poor."

He confronted the violent Merovingian kings over their crimes. The famous church of Saint-Germain-des-Prés in Paris, where he was buried, is named for him.
s369.intercession: St. Germanus of Paris, pray for us. Make us fathers and mothers to the poor. Amen.

s370.content:
Martin came from Pannonia, in today’s Hungary, and after a pilgrimage to the Holy Land went to Galicia in the far west of Spain. There he won the Suebi people from Arianism to the Catholic faith.

As archbishop of Braga, in today’s Portugal, he wrote On the Correction of Peasants, a practical guide to rooting out pagan superstitions among country people.
s370.intercession: St. Martin of Braga, pray for us. Bless the people of Portugal and Spain, and free us from every superstition. Amen.

s371.content:
Gregory came from a noble Gallo-Roman family full of bishops and became bishop of Tours, the great shrine of St. Martin. He protected his people and stood up to the violent Frankish kings.

His History of the Franks, in ten books, is our main source for the history of Gaul in the 6th century, and he wrote many lives of the saints.
s371.intercession: St. Gregory of Tours, pray for us. Bless historians, and help us to see God’s hand in history. Amen.

s372.content:
Leander was the eldest brother of St. Isidore, St. Fulgentius of Cartagena, and St. Florentina. As archbishop of Seville he befriended the future Pope St. Gregory the Great in Constantinople.

He led the Visigothic king Reccared and his people from Arianism to the Catholic faith at the Third Council of Toledo in 589, and introduced the Creed into the Mass in Spain.
s372.intercession: St. Leander, pray for us. Bless Spain, and bring all who are separated into the unity of the faith. Amen.

s373.content:
Venantius was an Italian poet who traveled to Gaul, where he became a friend and adviser of St. Radegund and her nuns in Poitiers. He later became bishop of Poitiers.

He wrote two of the greatest hymns of the Church, sung in Holy Week to this day: the "Vexilla Regis" ("The royal banners forward go") and the "Pange Lingua Gloriosi" on the triumph of the Cross.
s373.intercession: St. Venantius, pray for us. Teach us to glory in the Cross of Christ and to praise God in song. Amen.

s374.content:
Kentigern, affectionately called Mungo ("dear one"), was the apostle of the Britons of Strathclyde and founded the church at Glasgow, where his tomb lies in the cathedral.

A legend tells that he recovered a queen’s lost ring from the belly of a salmon, saving her life. The fish and ring still appear on the coat of arms of Glasgow.
s374.intercession: St. Kentigern, pray for us. Bless the city of Glasgow and all who seek God’s mercy. Amen.

s375.content:
Sophronius was a monk and scholar who became patriarch of Jerusalem. He led the defense of the teaching that Christ has two wills, human and divine, against the Monothelite heresy.

When the Arab armies besieged Jerusalem in 637, he negotiated the city’s surrender to Caliph Umar, protecting its churches and Christians. He died soon after.
s375.intercession: St. Sophronius, pray for us. Protect the Christians of the Holy Land, and help us to unite our will with God’s. Amen.

s376.content:
Maximus was a high official at the Byzantine court who became a monk. He was the greatest defender of the truth that Christ has a fully human will, freely united with His divine will.

He supported Pope St. Martin I at the Lateran Synod of 649. Arrested by the emperor, he had his tongue cut out and his right hand cut off so he could no longer speak or write, and he died in exile in Georgia.
s376.intercession: St. Maximus, pray for us. Help us to unite our will with Christ’s, and to confess the truth fearlessly. Amen.

s377.content:
Ildephonsus was a monk and abbot who became archbishop of Toledo. He wrote a celebrated treatise defending the perpetual virginity of Mary.

According to a beloved legend, Our Lady appeared to him in the cathedral and gave him a chasuble as a sign of her gratitude, a scene painted by El Greco, Velázquez, and many others.
s377.intercession: St. Ildephonsus, pray for us. Give us a tender love for the Virgin Mary. Amen.

s378.content:
Germanus was patriarch of Constantinople when the Emperor Leo III began the destruction of holy images in 726. He refused to support iconoclasm, saying he could not change the faith without an ecumenical council, and was forced from office.

He wrote beautiful homilies on the Virgin Mary and a commentary on the Divine Liturgy.
s378.intercession: St. Germanus, pray for us. Help us to honor the holy images that lead us to Christ and His saints. Amen.

s379.content:
Andrew was born in Damascus, became a monk in Jerusalem, and later archbishop of Gortyna in Crete. He was one of the great hymn writers of the Byzantine Church.

His Great Canon of Repentance, with 250 stanzas, is still sung in Eastern churches during Lent. It walks through the whole Bible, calling the soul to repentance.
s379.intercession: St. Andrew of Crete, pray for us. Give us true repentance and a love of the Scriptures. Amen.

s380.content:
Theodore was abbot of the great monastery of Stoudios in Constantinople, which he made a model of monastic reform with about a thousand monks.

During the second wave of iconoclasm he defended the veneration of holy images and was exiled, imprisoned, and beaten. He appealed to the pope in Rome for support.
s380.intercession: St. Theodore, pray for us. Help us to persevere in faith through persecution. Amen.

s381.content:
Anskar was a Benedictine monk from Corbie in France who volunteered for the mission to Denmark and Sweden, where he built the first churches.

As archbishop of Hamburg-Bremen he persevered through Viking raids that burned his cathedral and destroyed much of his work. He is called the "Apostle of the North."
s381.intercession: St. Anskar, pray for us. Bless the peoples of Scandinavia, and give us perseverance when our work seems to fail. Amen.

s382.content:
Ulrich was bishop of Augsburg for fifty years. He visited every parish, cared for the poor and sick, and helped rebuild after the Magyar invasions, defending the city during the siege of 955.

In 993 Pope John XV declared him a saint, the first known canonization by a pope.
s382.intercession: St. Ulrich, pray for us. Bless bishops who care for every part of their flock. Amen.

s383.content:
Wolfgang was a teacher and Benedictine monk who went as a missionary to the Hungarians before becoming bishop of Regensburg in Bavaria.

He reformed monasteries, cared for the poor, and was tutor to the future Emperor St. Henry II. He is especially loved in Austria and Bavaria.
s383.intercession: St. Wolfgang, pray for us. Bless teachers and those who form the leaders of tomorrow. Amen.

s384.content:
Stanislaus was bishop of Kraków when he rebuked King Bolesław II for his cruelty and immorality, and finally excommunicated him.

According to tradition, the king killed Stanislaus with his own hand while the bishop was celebrating Mass. He is a patron of Poland, and Pope St. John Paul II, his successor in Kraków, called him a patron of moral order.
s384.intercession: St. Stanislaus, pray for us. Give shepherds the courage to speak the truth to the powerful. Amen.

s385.content:
Malachy was archbishop of Armagh and the great reformer of the Church in Ireland. He restored the sacraments, built stone churches, and brought the Cistercians to Ireland, founding Mellifont Abbey.

He was a close friend of St. Bernard of Clairvaux, in whose arms he died, and Bernard wrote his life. The "Prophecy of the Popes" attributed to him is a later forgery.
s385.intercession: St. Malachy, pray for us. Renew the Church in Ireland and everywhere in holiness. Amen.

s386.content:
Lawrence was a king’s son, given as a hostage as a boy, who became abbot of Glendalough and then archbishop of Dublin. He fed the poor during famine and lived simply.

During the Norman invasion of Ireland he negotiated for peace and protected his people. He died in Normandy while seeking peace with King Henry II.
s386.intercession: St. Lawrence O’Toole, pray for us. Bless Dublin, and make us peacemakers. Amen.

s387.content:
Thomas was a Spanish Augustinian friar and university professor who became archbishop of Valencia. He gave nearly all his income to the poor, so that he was called "the Almsgiver" and "the Father of the Poor."

He even gave away his own bed shortly before his death. He was a great preacher and a reformer of his diocese.
s387.intercession: St. Thomas of Villanova, pray for us. Make us generous to the poor, holding nothing back. Amen.

s388.content:
John entered the monastery at the foot of Mount Sinai as a teenager and spent decades as a hermit before being made abbot. At the request of another abbot, he wrote The Ladder of Divine Ascent, describing the spiritual life as thirty rungs, from renouncing the world to faith, hope, and love.

The Ladder is read in Eastern monasteries every Lent, and the fourth Sunday of Great Lent is dedicated to him. His name, Climacus, means "of the Ladder."
s388.intercession: St. John of the Ladder, pray for us. Help us to climb toward God step by step, and never to give up. Amen.

s389.content:
Romanos was a deacon from Syria who served in Constantinople. According to tradition, he had no gift for singing until the Theotokos appeared to him in a dream on Christmas Eve and gave him a scroll to eat. The next morning he sang his famous Christmas kontakion, "Today the Virgin gives birth to the One above all being."

He is said to have written about a thousand hymns, and is honored as the greatest hymn writer of the Byzantine Church.
s389.intercession: St. Romanos, pray for us. Teach us to praise God with joyful song. Amen.

s390.content:
Symeon was a young official at the Byzantine court who became a monk and later abbot of the monastery of St. Mamas in Constantinople. He wrote with burning conviction about his experiences of the divine light and taught that every Christian is called to a living, conscious experience of God.

His hymns and discourses deeply shaped Eastern spirituality. He is one of only three saints the East calls "Theologian," alongside St. John the Evangelist and St. Gregory of Nazianzus.
s390.intercession: St. Symeon, pray for us. Kindle in us a living love for God. Amen.

s391.content:
Kuriakose was a priest of the Syro-Malabar Church in Kerala, India. He co-founded the first Indian religious congregation for men, the Carmelites of Mary Immaculate, and a congregation for women.

He set up a seminary and a printing press, and asked that a school be opened beside every church, bringing education to the poor of every caste. He was canonized in 2014.
s391.intercession: St. Kuriakose Elias, pray for us. Bless Christian families and all who teach the young. Amen.

s392.content:
Alphonsa was a Franciscan Clarist sister of the Syro-Malabar Church in Kerala. As a young girl she burned her feet in a fire pit to escape an arranged marriage, and she suffered almost constant illness for the rest of her short life.

She accepted her pain with peace and offered it for others, and many visitors found comfort at her bedside. In 2008 she became the first woman of Indian origin to be canonized.
s392.intercession: St. Alphonsa, pray for us. Help the sick to unite their sufferings with Christ in peace. Amen.

s393.content:
Euphrasia was a Carmelite sister of the Syro-Malabar Church who spent much of her life as superior of a convent in Ollur, Kerala. She spent long hours before the Blessed Sacrament.

The people of the town called her "the Praying Mother," and came to her for prayers and counsel. She was canonized in 2014.
s393.intercession: St. Euphrasia, praying mother, pray for us. Teach us to stay close to Jesus in prayer. Amen.

s394.content:
Nimatullah was a Maronite monk and priest of the Lebanese Maronite Order. He taught theology for many years, and among his students was St. Charbel Makhlouf.

He was known for his humility, his devotion to the Blessed Sacrament and the Virgin Mary, and his love of manual work, binding books for the monastery. He was canonized in 2004.
s394.intercession: St. Nimatullah, pray for us. Bless teachers, and help us to seek holiness in our daily work. Amen.

s395.content:
Ignatius was the Armenian Catholic archbishop of Mardin in today’s Turkey. During the Armenian Genocide in 1915, he was arrested with hundreds of his people and ordered to convert to Islam.

He refused, encouraged his flock to remain faithful, and was shot after celebrating a last Eucharist with them. He was beatified in 2001 and canonized in 2025.
s395.intercession: St. Ignatius Maloyan, pray for us. Strengthen persecuted Christians, and bless the Armenian people. Amen.

s396.content:
Leonid was a Russian Orthodox seminarian who became Catholic and was ordained a priest of the Byzantine rite. In 1917 he was named the first exarch of the Russian Greek Catholic Church.

Under the Soviets he was imprisoned for years, including in the Solovki labor camp, where he ministered to fellow prisoners. He died in exile, worn out by suffering, and was beatified as a martyr in 2001.
s396.intercession: Blessed Leonid, pray for us. Work for the unity of Christians of East and West. Amen.

s397.content:
Emilian was a married Ukrainian Greek Catholic priest and the father of six children. During the Nazi occupation he gave hundreds of Jews baptismal certificates to protect them, and he was arrested for helping them.

In the Majdanek concentration camp he served the prisoners of every faith as a priest until he died in 1944. He was beatified in 2001, and has been recognized as Righteous of Ukraine.
s397.intercession: Blessed Emilian, pray for us. Give us courage to protect the persecuted and to serve all people. Amen.

s398.content:
Theodore was the young bishop of Mukachevo for the Ruthenian Greek Catholic Church when the Soviets took over the region after the Second World War. He refused to separate his Church from Rome.

In 1947 his carriage was rammed by a truck in a staged accident. He survived, but was poisoned in the hospital and died at thirty-six. He was beatified in 2001.
s398.intercession: Blessed Theodore, pray for us. Strengthen the Church in her loyalty to the successor of Peter. Amen.

s399.content:
Vasyl was a Ukrainian Greek Catholic Redemptorist priest who was secretly ordained a bishop while the Soviet Union had outlawed his Church. He spent years in Soviet prisons and labor camps.

Released and expelled, he died in Winnipeg, Canada, where his relics are honored today. He was beatified as a martyr in 2001.
s399.intercession: Blessed Vasyl, pray for us. Strengthen all who suffer for the faith under persecution. Amen.

s400.content:
Boris and Gleb were young princes of Kyiv, sons of St. Vladimir the Great. When their father died, their older brother Sviatopolk sent men to kill them to seize the throne.

Both refused to raise an army against their brother, choosing to die rather than shed Christian blood. They were the first saints honored in Kyivan Rus’, venerated as "passion-bearers," those who accepted an unjust death in imitation of Christ.
s400.intercession: Holy passion-bearers Boris and Gleb, pray for us. Teach us to choose peace and to forgive those who harm us. Amen.
